ordered_diagnoses: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Ear

facts.raw_span: a 2-year history of an enlarging, intermittently painful, purplish lump in her left ear canal
cracking and pus-filled sores at the site
a 3.5 × 2.5 cm purplish-red mass in the left external ear canal
irregular, friable surface and bleeding on minimal contact
Contrast-enhanced CT of the mastoids showed a lobulated mass in the cutis and subcutis of the left auricle
extending into the external acoustic canal and into the left parotid space
bilateral level II–IV cervical lymph nodes up to 0.6 cm in diameter
CT angiography demonstrated marked vascularity of the mass
supplied by branches of the left superficial temporal and posterior auricular arteries
Incisional biopsy revealed atypical cells and granulomatous inflammation
a provisional diagnosis of an auricular malignant tumor without a clear histopathological subtype

concepts.why: The patient has a 2-year history of an enlarging, intermittently painful, purplish lump in her left ear canal, with a lobulated mass in the cutis and subcutis of the left auricle, and incisional biopsy revealed atypical cells and granulomatous inflammation.

concepts.preferred_label: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Ear
concepts.why: The patient has a purplish-red mass in the left external ear canal with an irregular, friable surface and bleeding on minimal contact, which is consistent with squamous cell carcinoma.
The patient has a highly vascular mass in the left ear canal, which is consistent with angiosarcoma, a malignant tumor that arises from blood vessels.
The patient has a history of cracking and pus-filled sores at the site, and incisional biopsy revealed granulomatous inflammation, which is consistent with granulomatous disease.
The patient has a highly vascular mass in the left ear canal with bleeding on minimal contact, which is consistent with vascular malformation.
The finding of a highly vascular mass extending into the external acoustic canal and into the left parotid space, as seen on imaging, is consistent with a hemangioma.

rationales.F01: The patient's 2-year history of an enlarging, intermittently painful, purplish lump in her left ear canal suggests a possible malignant tumor.
rationales.F03: The presence of a 3.5 × 2.5 cm purplish-red mass in the left external ear canal is highly suggestive of a malignant tumor.
rationales.F04: The irregular, friable surface and bleeding on minimal contact of the mass are characteristic of malignant tumors.
rationales.F08: The marked vascularity of the mass, as demonstrated by CT angiography, is consistent with a highly vascularized malignant tumor such as angiosarcoma.
rationales.F09: The blood supply to the mass from branches of the left superficial temporal and posterior auricular arteries is consistent with a malignant tumor.
rationales.F10: The presence of atypical cells and granulomatous inflammation on incisional biopsy is highly suggestive of a malignant tumor.
